title: skeleton-index-sidebar-rewrite-grooming
summary: Working notes for a lightweight, index-first redesign of the console left sidebar and page hierarchy. Focus: reduce noise, create task-centric entry points, and make routes predictable for deep-linking and rollouts.
goals: Reduce top-level items from ~12 to 6-8 by introducing a skeletal index and task hubs
Provide deterministic deep links for rollouts and canary routes with stable URL paths
Improve discoverability of mission-critical flows (deploys, logs, rollouts, metrics) in 2 taps
Make left rail permission-aware and progressively disclosed to avoid cognitive load for new users
constraints: Must be backward-compatible with existing permalinks used in audits and support tickets
Rollouts and canaries must continue to be addressable via query params for A/B experiments
Console must support both narrow mobile widths and wide desktop; sidebar collapses to an index chip on small widths
Telemetry hooks need to be non-blocking and emit before route transitions for funnel analysis
proposed_structure: SKELETAL INDEX (left-most): single compact index that expands to show context-specific hubs
MICRO-HUBS: group related pages (Models, Deployments, Routing, Observability) under a shallow hub
TASK ENTRY PANELS: Secondary panel surfaces contextual tasks (new deployment, stage rollout, add API key) without full route change
BREADCRUMBS + CANONICAL URL: every micro-hub expands to canonical path /hub/:hubName and subroute /hub/:hubName/:resource
PERSISTENT QUICK-ACTIONS: top-level action menu (Create, Query, Evaluate) accessible from any route
wireframe_notes: Index collapsed state shows 1-letter glyphs + hover labels; tap/hover opens skeletal index overlay
When a hub is opened, the index pins the hub with a subtle blue left border (not full page reflow)
Task panels slide over current content (non-modal) and keep the backstack for browser history
Use a thin caret chevron to indicate micro-hub expansion rather than full nested list to reduce perceived depth
Route transition animation should be <120ms fade/slide to maintain perceived high performance
Add small context chips next to hub labels showing counts (e.g., Deployments · 3 active) — opt-in via org setting
access_and_permissions: Resolve edge-case: collapsed index must not reveal item names for which user lacks Read access
When permissions change mid-session (SSO role update), re-evaluate index and silently remap active route if needed
Super-admins get experimental toggle to view hidden hubs for troubleshooting
grooming_backlog: P0: canonical-route-mapping PRD (owner: Aisha Patel) — produce final mapping table and param schema
P0: skeleton-index component (owner: Ethan Morris) — prototype collapsed/expanded interactions
P1: breadcrumb canonicalization middleware (owner: Ravi Kapoor) — ensure old permalinks redirect with 301 semantics
P1: telemetry schema for navigation events (owner: Lina Chen) — define events: index_open, hub_open, task_panel_open, route_change
P2: accessibility pass (owner: UX Accessibility team) — keyboard nav, screen reader labels, focus traps
P2: micro-hub count chips feature flag (owner: Product Analytics) — AB test cognitive load impact
P3: mobile index overlay polish (owner: Mobile Console UX) — optimize animation + hit target sizes
decisions_made: Adopt index-first pattern instead of deep multi-level nesting to flatten IA and improve discoverability
URLs will prefer path-based semantics (/hub/:hub/:id) and use query params only for experiments and ephemeral filters
Task panels will not create new top-level routes; they will push state into history but maintain parent canonical path
Micro-hubs will be surfaced based on usage frequency and role — dynamic ordering behind a flag
open_questions: How do we present overlapping hubs (eg: a Model that is both in 'Models' and 'Deployments') — single canonical hub or cross-links?
What is the migration path for customers who have bookmarks to deeply-nested legacy routes older than 18 months?
Should micro-hub counts be eventually consistent or precise — cost/latency vs. UX tradeoff?
When a user collapses the index, should we persist preference per-device, per-user, or per-org by default?
next_steps: Schedule 60m cross-functional workshop (owners: Lina + Aisha) to finalize route table — target: 2025-02-24
Ship index prototype to feature branch and demo in Friday sync (owner: Ethan) — target: 2025-02-28
Create migration doc for Support with redirect map and FAQs (owner: Ravi) — draft due 2025-03-04

notes_to_reviewers: This doc is intentionally focused on the 'index-first' experiment. Looking for feedback on canonical URL semantics, permission edge-cases, and whether task panels should be bookmarkable. Add comments or tag owners in linked Confluence page.
